newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-STUTTGART HIT BY INJURIES BEFORE BAYERN CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-STUTTGART HIT BY INJURIES BEFORE BAYERN CLASH.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart have been hit by injuries and off-the-field problems in the run-up to Sunday's top-of-the-table clash with German first division leaders Bayern Munich.
Euro 96 striker Fredi Bobic has been told he cannot train until Sunday because of an infection and defender Thomas Schneider is almost certain to miss the game because of ligament problems.

Dutch libero Frank Verlaat is also struggling with a muscle strain and it is not clear whether Croat midfielder Zvonimir Soldo will be able to return to Germany from Zagreb in time for the game following the death of his father.
Bayern, by contrast, have most of their top players fit. But the tension in the Munich camp is clearly high ahead of the Stuttgart clash which will be played in front of a capacity 53,000 crowd.
Bayern had a keenly contested seven-a-side game in training on Friday which forced normally subdued coach Giovanni Trapattoni to lose his temper.
"Sometimes the players don's listen and I have to shout," said Trapattoni. "This game is particulary important. We can prove something on Sunday and every player knows what it is all about."

Bayern, who have a two-point lead over second-placed Stuttgart with two games remaining before the winter break, will be without their international playmaker Mehmet Scholl but in-form midfielder Mario Basler has recovered from a stomach upset.
Goalkeeper Oliver Kahn and wing back Christian Ziege, both German internationals, have also recovered from injuries.
Despite Stuttgart's superb form this season, coach Joachim Loew is playing down his team's chances.
"Bayern have been top class for generations," Loew said. "In that respect, they are used to matches like Sunday's. Bayern are always strong when they have their backs to the wall."

VfB Stuttgart - 1-Franz Wohlfahrt, 14-Thomas Schneider (2-Hendrik Herzog), 5-Frank Verlaat, 4-Thomas Berthold, 7-Matthias Hagner, 20-Zvonimir Soldo (6-Franco Foda), 10-Krasimir Balakov, 16-Gerhard Poschner, 3-Thorsten Legat, 9-Giovane Elber, 11-Fredi Bobic

Bayern Munich - 1-Oliver Kahn. 10-Lothar Matthaeus, 15-Samuel Kuffour, 5-Thomas Helmer, 7-Mario Basler, 16-Dieter Hamann, 8-Thomas Strunz, 6-Christian Nerlinger, 17-Christian Ziege, 18-Juergen Klinsmann, 21-Alexander Zickler
